decisions.choice: This repository becomes the hosted DinkusKit coupon service: a Cloudflare Worker with one Durable Object per store holding coupon records and redemption attempts, called by Commerce checkout over HTTPS at one fixed host with a scoped JWT. Commerce keeps owning prices, cart, checkout, order, money, tax and refunds; the service evaluates only Commerce-priced lines and never trusts browser prices or totals. If the service is unavailable the coupon is unavailable and checkout continues without it; an accepted discount still fails closed per checkout-total-preservation.

decisions.question: Where do coupons live for Registry stores now that Commerce's Registry build cannot carry them?
decisions.rationale: Registry caps each plugin file at 128 KiB and commerce#75 removed coupons from Commerce's Registry build. EmDash 1.2 has no plugin-to-plugin call, and allowedHosts has no same-site token (exact host, *.suffix or bare *), so a same-site Coupons plugin would need Commerce to reach any host. Payments and Inventory already use the hosted pattern.

decisions.choice: Run Commerce's coupon core unchanged from an exact copy, under vendor/commerce, of the Commerce files the build needs, taken from the commit in package.json dinkuskit.commercePin. CI (npm run check:pin) fails if any copied file differs from Commerce at that commit, and the copy is never edited. Implement CouponCollection over Durable Object storage and CouponCatalogStorage in memory from the priced lines Commerce sends. Pin bumps are their own PR with contract tests re-run.

decisions.question: Where do merchants manage coupons for Registry stores?
decisions.rationale: Every DinkusKit plugin must be a Registry plugin, and the admin screens were about 8.6 KB of Commerce's bundle that no longer fits there.

decisions.choice: Add admin preview and confirm routes under coupons:admin: POST /coupons/previews returns before/after and a single-use confirmation that lasts five minutes and is bound to the store, the exact request and, for disable or enable, the coupon's current revision; POST /coupons/commands commits it under a caller-chosen command id; an exact retry returns the first result, results are kept 30 days, and GET /coupons/commands/{id} reads them. Merit refusals (INVALID_INPUT, NOT_FOUND, REVISION_CONFLICT, CODE_IN_USE) are stored and use up the confirmation; confirmation-gate refusals store nothing. First actions: create, disable, enable. The direct admin routes stay; the admin plugin chooses which to use when it is built.

decisions.question: How does the coupon service let a script or agent change coupons so a person approves the exact change first?
decisions.rationale: DinkusKit CLIs never offer --force: Inventory and Commerce make every change go through a server-side preview a person confirms, and recover lost answers by command id. Binding the preview in the service, not the CLI, means the confirmed change is exactly what runs, including the rule id and start time the service fills in.

decisions.choice: dinkus-coupons ships in this repository on the shared DinkusKit CLI kernel, outside every plugin bundle, with: coupons list, show (with use counts), create, disable, enable, and commands show and resolve; coupons edit is listed as planned and sends nothing. Changes need --site on the command line and the service's preview, confirmed by typing the value or with --no-input --confirm; there is no --force. The pass comes only from DINKUS_COUPONS_TOKEN and is never sent to an endpoint from project config; there is no built-in production endpoint. Amounts are USD. Contract: docs/CLI-SPEC.md.

decisions.question: What does the first dinkus-coupons command-line tool do, and under which rules?
decisions.rationale: Ronald chose the command-line tool before the admin plugin on 2026-10-10. It follows the create-cli pattern and the token and confirmation rules already locked for the Commerce and Inventory CLIs, and costs no Registry bundle bytes.

decisions.choice: plugins/coupons-admin ships one sandboxed Registry plugin (slug dinkus-coupons, name Coupons, no native entry) with one admin page, Coupons, and network:request limited to coupons.dinkuskit.com; no storage collections. Its admin route needs plugins:manage and a signed-in administrator on an admin page. Its only setting is the store's coupons:admin pass, saved as an encrypted secret; the store comes from the pass and the service address is fixed. Screens: coupon list (25 a page, newest first), coupon page (terms plus uses allowed, used, held by checkouts in progress, left), create, edit (code, discount, products, sale items, minimum spend, first and last day, time zone, total uses), turn off and turn on; no delete. Days are whole days in a picked time zone (US zones and UTC, plus a coupon's own zone); a blank first day starts now; an edit keeps the exact time of a day it leaves alone. Every change goes through the service's preview and needs a confirm click from the same administrator within five minutes; the plugin keeps the pending change and its command id in plugin KV for up to a day, so Check again after a lost answer never repeats a change. Before calling, the plugin explains a missing, unreadable, checkout-only, hour-old or refused pass and links to settings; renewing passes waits for the dinkuskit.com sign-in service.

decisions.question: What does the first Coupons admin Registry plugin do, and how does it reach the coupon service?
decisions.rationale: Ronald chose Coupon admin on 2026-10-10: the CLI first, then the admin plugin. Registry first, the locked coupon-admin-registry-plugin boundary, and the preview and confirm rule already used by the CLI and the Inventory plugin; about 24 KB, far under the 128 KiB per-file limit.

decisions.choice: The admin preview routes add action edit: { couponId, changes } naming at least one of code, globalCap and rule, where rule holds only the fields it replaces whole (discount, appliesTo, selectedProductIds, includeSaleItems, minimumEligibleMerchandise, startsAt, endsAt, timeZone). The preview fixes the whole next rule (same rule id, version plus one), is bound to the coupon's revision like disable and enable, and an edit to the values the coupon already has is 409 NO_CHANGE; turning off and on stay their own actions. Every admin answer (list, get, create, edit, disable, previews, commands) gives coupons without their redemption attempts; counts report consumed, held and left.

decisions.question: What does the coupon service change so the admin plugin can edit coupons and load busy ones?
decisions.rationale: The plugin's edit screen needs a previewed edit. Admin answers carried every redemption attempt, so one busy coupon could push the list past EmDash's 8 MiB limit on a plugin's network answer; nothing read the attempts from these answers.
